g_roast: Twelve years on the brigade, hermanos, and no crew of mine ever ran toward the smoke this happily and this badly.
My mother cleans offices, and she would organise this party better with one hand and a mop.
g_fire_back: Ay, hermano, that's beautiful, coming from the one who set his own boots on fire last night.
Big talk, from someone who dances worse than me, and I dance like a shopping trolley with one bad wheel.
g_pile_on: And then they tried to put out the grass fire by stamping on it. In sandals, hermanos.
Oh, the true story is uglier. They asked the innkeeper to dance, and she pretended to be a coat stand.
lines.g_peacemake: Ya, ya, hermanos, sit down, both of you. My mother settled every fight on our street with a plate of empanadas, and I'm doing the same.
lines.g_take_side: Sorry, hermano, I'm with this one. My mother would side with them too, and she has never once been wrong.
lines.g_left_out: You two are cooking something private, fine by me. I'll go teach somebody to dance badly.
lines.g_include: Come, hermano, sit with us. In Valparaiso nobody eats alone, the neighbours would phone your mother.
lines.g_bad_plan: My plan, hermanos, is very simple. We run straight in shouting, and if it goes badly, I blame whoever agreed with me.
lines.g_plan_yes: Eso, that's a good plan, I love it. I go in first, you follow, and nobody goes back without me.
lines.g_plan_no: No, hermano, that plan burns us all. The wind turns at noon, and we'd be on the wrong side of it.
lines.g_hype: Vamos, hermanos, chins up and stay together. Nobody gets left behind, and we go now.
lines.g_toast: A toast, a short one, my mother would kill me for a long one. To my hermanos, who always come back out.
lines.g_cheers: Salud, hermanos, to your health, and to whoever's dancing with me later.
g_quiet_line: The stars here are good, but the ones over the port at home are better. I'm allowed to be biased.
Somebody left the cookfire smouldering. I put it out properly, no need to thank me.
lines.g_after_wipe: Okay, okay, up, everybody, slowly, count yourselves. We got knocked flat, it happens, and next time we're smarter about it.
lines.g_crew: On the brigade we were a family, ten of us on one truck. I never thought I'd find that twice, and look at us.
lines.g_exasperated: Twice I told you to wait, and I even did the hand signal my mother uses on taxis. And every one of you charged anyway.
lines.g_love_sharp: You see trouble coming before anybody. My mother has that, she knew I'd broken a window before I got home.
lines.g_love_kind: You look after the scared ones first, always. My mother would adopt you, hermano, no question.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh, and I'm the loud one, so that's a big achievement. My mother would love you.
lines.g_love_brave: You charge back into the smoke for people, no hesitation. Hermano, you belong on a brigade.
lines.g_love_steady: You don't panic when everything goes wrong. I panic very loudly, so I really admire it.
lines.g_love_clever: You plan three moves ahead, hermano. I plan zero moves ahead, so together we're a genius.
lines.g_love_honest: You tell me straight when I'm being an idiot. Only my mother does that, and she does it every day.
lines.g_love_quiet: You're quiet and I'm loud, and somehow it works perfectly. Like my mother and her kitchen radio, hermano.
lines.g_love_fierce: You hold on when everyone else breaks. That's how my mother raised me on her own, by being too stubborn to quit.
lines.g_love_warm: Being with you is like a fiesta on the hill, music, empanadas, everybody dancing badly. I missed that so much.
g_loved: Ay, hermano, stop it, the soot on my face is running now. In front of everybody, again.
That's beautiful, gracias, and I'm telling my mother you said it.
lines.g_hate_sharp: Your tongue is always looking for a wound. On my street, people like that ate alone at the fiesta.
lines.g_hate_kind: Stop telling me to be careful, hermano, please. My mother says it enough for the whole world.
lines.g_hate_funny: I love a joke, believe me, but not when somebody's hurt. Then you shut up and you help.
lines.g_hate_brave: You charge at everything with your eyes shut. Brave is beautiful, stupid gets people hurt, hermano.
lines.g_hate_steady: You wait and wait, and the moment leaves without you. Sometimes you just move, hermano.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain things to me like I'm a child. I'm loud, hermano, not slow.
lines.g_hate_honest: Everything comes out of your mouth, no filter. Some things you keep in your pocket, hermano.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You never say anything, and then we all have to guess what you need. Shout a little, hermano, it's healthy.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything is a competition with you, even who dances first. Dancing isn't a contest, and I'd lose anyway.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk even more than me, and that's saying something. Give my ears one quiet hour.
lines.g_respect: We don't get along, hermano, and that's fine. But you held the line back there, and I respect that.
lines.g_call_out: That one was yours, hermano, sorry. I said hold, and you didn't hold, and the whole thing came apart.
lines.g_stung: Okay, okay, I hear you, hermano. I'll go for a walk and write my mother a letter about it.
lines.g_concede: You read it right, hermano, and I didn't. I thought about it all day, and you were right.
lines.g_nod: You too, hermano, good work up there. We don't need to make a fiesta of it.
lines.g_callback_save: I haven't forgotten you pulled me out of that one. On the brigade, you'd get my last empanada forever.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me, last ones on our feet, covered in soot head to toe. Best fiesta of my life, hermano.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you shouted at me that time, I sulked for a whole shift. Then I saw you were right, chucha.
lines.g_former_rivals: At the start I thought you'd leave me behind. Now you'd get my last empanada, hermano, and I don't give those away.
lines.g_changed: I used to charge in ahead of everyone, alone. Lately I wait for the crew, and it feels strange and good.
g_unguarded: Just between us, hermano. The hellfire found a firefighter, and it's a joke at my expense, so I laugh at it. Mostly I laugh at it.
I dance cueca at every fiesta, and I'm terrible at it. That's the whole point, hermano, you dance anyway.
lines.g_clipped: Okay, hermano, your call. I'll be at the front.
lines.g_noticed_open: Eso, look at this, a whole story out loud. Keep going, hermano, my mother would already be crying.
arg_ask: {player}, hermano, you decide this one, please. We've both shouted, and nobody's listening.
Captain {player}, this one's yours. Make the call, and the shouting stops.
lines.arg_backed_me: Eso, gracias, {player}. My mother didn't raise a fool, and neither did yours.
lines.arg_backed_them: Okay, okay, your call, hermano. I still think you're wrong, but I love you anyway.
lines.arg_stayed_out: You don't pick a side, eh? Smart, very smart, my mother would approve.
lines.arg_always_their_side: They win the call again, {player}, every argument. I'm loud, hermano, not blind.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody's deciding, so I decide, like a captain. I'm right, and we move.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, hermano, I can't do that one. I know how it ends, and it isn't pretty.
lines.arg_grumble: I still think I was right, but okay. I'll only complain about it in my letters home.
lines.arg_settled: Half right each, hermano, fine, fine. We shake hands and go eat.
lines.seen_listens: You let a loud man finish talking, {player}. That's rare, believe me, I've tested it.
lines.seen_truth: You speak plain, {player}, no decoration. My mother talks like that, and she's always right.
lines.seen_jokes: In the worst moments you make everybody laugh, {player}. On the brigade we did that at four in the morning, and it saved us.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep out of the fights, {player}. Smart, smarter than me, I jump in every one.
lines.seen_biased: The best gear always lands in the same hands, {player}. Even I notice, and I notice nothing.
lines.seen_harsh: Your words can sting, {player}. My skin's like an old boot, but some of this crew are softer.
lines.seed_right: What you told me after that bad fire, {player}, I hated it. Today I did it your way, and the line held.
lines.seed_remember: Still thinking about what you said when it all fell apart. Haven't decided yet, hermano.
lines.seed_wrong: I tried it your way, {player}, and it went worse. I tell you so you know, hermano, nothing more.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Hermano, you got a minute? That one was close, very close, and I'm not saying it to the others.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: We all went down, the whole crew. Sit with me, and we go back over every moment of it, no shouting, I promise.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} dropped first, and reading the fire is my job, hermano. I should have seen her turning, {player}.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: Start to finish, everybody walked out. On the brigade, that's the best day there is, hermano.
lines.talk_development: Strange question, hermano, don't laugh. Am I different? I wait for people now, and I never used to.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been loud with {name}, too loud. In my family we shout to say we love you, and not everybody knows that.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: An honest read, {player}. Would {name} miss me on the line, or do I just smell like smoke to them?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} is a hot wind in my face, {player}, every day. But in a bad fight, they're the one I'd want on my flank.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name} isn't right, {player}. They've gone quiet like my mother before a storm, and I don't like it.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: One thing, {player}, straight, hermano to hermano. The best kit keeps landing on {name}, and the whole camp sees it.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I'll say it to your face, it's better. Me and {name} are fire and dry grass, and I'm tired of pretending otherwise.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep heading into fires with no escape route, {player}. I'll go anywhere you say, but I want a way out.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: I got {name} wrong, {player}. They read it right and I didn't, and I say it now before my pride catches fire.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: A straight question, hermano. When the big fire comes, I'm left at the station. Is that the strategy, or does the captain not trust me with a hose?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My gear was handed to {name} behind my back, hermano. I'd have passed it over myself, {player}, if you'd just asked me.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Gracias, hermano, that helps. Let's eat something.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: I'll be fine, I always walk out of it. She hasn't caught me yet.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: That's not what I needed to hear, hermano. I'll go walk it off.
lines.talk_lands_development: So you see it too, eh? Good, then it's real.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe so, maybe not, it's early. Ask me after the next fiesta.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, hermano, that's not it. You've read me wrong this time.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Okay, that's fair. I'll sit down with {name}, quietly, I promise.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Maybe, who knows. People are a mystery, hermano, and my mother says I'm the biggest one.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Forget I said it, please. And nothing to {name}, okay?
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Okay, that's fair, I take it. A little bruised, but I heal fast.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Okay, {player}, I heard. I'll chew on it at the next watch.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: Okay, so that's the answer. Good to know, hermano.
lines.talk_door_closed: No, hermano, I'm done with this one. I'll be dancing somewhere if you need me.
lines.arc_cracks: Today I let the young ones cut the firebreak without me, and they did it, hermano. I watched from the back. I've never watched from the back.
lines.arc_turn: For twelve years I thought the line holds because I'm on it. Maybe the line holds because I trained people, and that's a bigger thing.
lines.arc_become: I'm not the one who goes in first any more, hermano, I'm the one who teaches them how. And they're good, they're so good.
lines.arc_failed: Ah, I can't stand at the back, it's not in me. I'll keep going in first, and they'll keep following.
lines.alt_turn: The fire inside me got away from me today, {player}, only a little, only for a second. I didn't laugh about it this time.
lines.alt_become: I keep the fire on a short leash now, always. No jokes about it. I'm scared of her, hermano, and I should be.
g_roast_after: Still the worst brigade I ever had, hermanos, and I'd walk into any fire with every one of you.
Loud, messy, terrible dancers, all of you, and I wouldn't change a single face.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Up, everybody, together, nobody stays in the smoke. We fell, we cut a new line, and this time the crew leads.
lines.g_toast_after: To my brigade, the one that holds the line without me. Nothing I ever built is better, hermanos.
lines.g_crew_after: This is my brigade now, all of you. I don't go in alone any more, I go in with family.
g_quiet_line_after: I stood at the back today and the line held anyway. My mother would faint.
Called the young tauren in for dinner tonight, and every one of them came. My mother would be so proud.
g_loved_after: Gracias, hermano, really, no joke this time. I keep that one.
Ay, that's beautiful, and I believe you. Don't tell my mother I cried.

history.open: This yellow helmet, hermano? Twelve years with the forest fire brigade in Valparaiso. I landed in the Barrens in the middle of a grass fire, still wearing it.

options.text: And you walked out of the fire.
options.reply: I walked out, yes. Some days I say that like a joke, some days I don't. Today it's a joke.

options.text: A firefighter with hellfire. That's ironic.
options.reply: Ha, hermano, you see it too! It's a joke at my expense, so I decided to laugh first.
Every day, the whole crew, the broken motorbike, the bad coffee. So I'm building a new one here.

history.open: At Camp Taurajo I'm training a dozen young tauren to cut firebreaks, hermano. They're scared of fire, the ones from Mulgore, and they have every reason to be.

options.reply: One fire at a time. You show them she can be beaten, and then you let them beat her. Trust is built that way, slowly.

options.text: A brigade in the Barrens. That's huge.
options.reply: One in every town, that's the dream. My mother would say I'm getting ideas above my station. She's right, and I love it.

history.open: In 2024 the hills above Valparaiso burned for days, hermano. I spent four days on the line above my mother's house, no sleep, while the city burned below.

options.reply: It was still standing when I came down. I've never told anyone how close it was. Now I told you.
Four days, yes, and I'd do it again tomorrow. She sent empanadas up the hill with a neighbour. Cold, but the best I ever ate.

friend.open: When I landed in that grass fire, hermano, I wasn't alone. Others came through with me. I was the only one who walked out. I think about them every time I light a camp.

options.reply: Maybe not, hermano. My head knows that, and my heart is slower. Thank you for saying it.

options.text: That's why you go back in.
options.reply: Yes, exactly, every single time. You see me very clearly, hermano.

sworn.open: On the brigade, hermano, you'd follow your partner into any fire, no questions. I'd follow you into any fire. There's nothing bigger I can tell you.

options.reply: Eso, then we're brigade, forever. My mother is going to love you.
Ay, hermano, you sound exactly like her. Okay, okay, for you, I'll try.

reconciled.open: {name} and I talked it out, properly, no shouting, I promise. We're good now, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: Gracias, hermano, really. It feels better, like rain after the dry season.
A little shouting, at the start. Then we laughed. That's how you know it's finished.
